text: The location of the hotel itself was great as it was about a 2-3 block walk from the French Quarter. It was nice as the smells and crowds of the French Quarter didn't travel to the hotel. The hotel room itself was fine - nothing spectacular. We booked a double occupancy room which ended up being tucked WAY in the back of the hotel building. Because we were hidden away, our room was skipped for cleaning on one of the days. Not cool. When we pulled back the curtains of the very small window we had, all we saw were the windows of the other rooms that had the same view, a massive drain pipe, and the parking garage. So, natural light was not something we had much of. The bathroom was weird - the shower only had HALF a door. Imagine a shower with a sliding door, usually the part that moves and the part that doesn't are two separate pieces of glass. This shower only had the non-moving piece of glass installed so when you showered, water could easily flood the bathroom floor. Since we booked the room via Rocketmiles, we already paid for the hotel ahead of time. However, about a week later, we received a $200 charge from the hotel - no bill or statement about these extra charges so we tried calling the hotel for three days straight - no answer. Even tried checking different sites via Google to make sure we had the right number - all listed the same number. Got in touch with Rocketmiles to explain what had happened and if they could possibly get in touch with Omni for us - success! HOWEVER, when they told us what the charge was, it was not pleasing. They told us the charge was for parking - valet parking for 5 nights, $39.20/per night. Great! An explanation. BUT WE DID NOT BRING A CAR. We flew in from Boston and took a cab to and from the airport and have the receipts to prove it. No idea if it was a complete mistake on the hotel's part or if the people in the room next to us gave our room number, but during checkout, there should have been a final summary of charges if there was anything extra other than what we initially paid for. Since we weren't given any final papers, we checked to make sure our check-out was complete and they said it was. We will never consider staying at this location again.

text: PROS: I can see. CONS: Process slows down once you pay. Be prepared for high-pressure tactics asking you to leave a positive review. I've been thinking about LASIK surgery for 20 years, yes 2-0. Fear of all things eyeball kept me from taking the plunge, but I finally felt fed-up with my contacts. I narrowed down the surgery to Dr. Loden & Dr. Wang. I think they are both fine choices. THE CONSULTATION: I started with the seminar (25% off), which you will need because apparently for the price of LASIK you could buy a used car. The consultation takes 2.5 hours. During that time, they numb your eyes, poke, prod them, & torture them with various lights & apparatuses. They were understanding about the fact that the process sucks & to their credit, I was never sitting around waiting. They then connect you with a patient coordinator who hands you the price tag & suggests which way to go before you are passed to Dr. Wang. He will look over your test results, look at your eyeballs, & tell you everything you've already read on his website but in a soft-spoken manner. THE POST-CONSULTATION PHASE: For some reason, I started panicking after the consultation. Dr. Wang had mentioned that most of his patients get plugs that will dissolve. According to the internet :), plugs should be used as a last resort. Then I found an article about a whistle-blower doctor who blew the lid on a LASIK center for up-charging customers for plugs in the name of profit. To be blunt, this made me lose a lot of trust & I felt sick to my stomach and nervous. I ended up emailing my concerns to Dr. Wang's office, & he called me that night. During our call, I voiced my concerns about the plugs & also other things that I had started to freak out about. After reading on the internet (don't do that) I also started panicking about flap LASIK vs PRK non-flap surgery. And I really wanted PRK. I was able to talk to Dr. Wang about both concerns. The fact that he personally called me & had zero ego about my concerns meant a lot. He explained that plugs are preventative & as so many people have dry eye after surgery, they're worth it. He said I could choose the surgery I wanted (PRK or LASIK), & to let them know what I wanted the day of. THE SURGERY: The day of the surgery I was scheduled to come in at 10:30, I didn't leave until 2:30 = long day. I arrived, they got me in, I told them I wanted PRK, they talked me out of it :). I ended up getting LASIK. They confirmed my prescription & asked me to finalize my payment. I did. Then things slowed down. Ironically or because they had my money? I will never know. But my husband & I did have a good laugh about it. We waited and waited and when they called me again, it was time. They had given me a Valium in advance, it didn't do a damn thing. I told them so, they told me I'd be fine. Did it hurt? No. Was it uncomfortable? At times, it was. A Valium that worked would have been welcome. The clamping of the eye isn't pleasant, & then they do this suction thing which makes everything go black. I'm not going to lie, I flat-out panicked. I wasn't calm, but tried to use yogic breathing, & I managed to stay still enough that it was over before I knew it. I had a teddy bear & a husband. I recommend bringing both if you can as they brought me a lot of comfort. When the surgery was over, I was in complete shock, & I was shaking from hyperventilating during my panic attack. Even though I expressed that I was dizzy, they tried to hurry me off the bed. They moved me to another chair to insert plugs. Before I had even left the operating room, they had another patient in the bed prepping for her procedure. I wasn't into this part at all. Seems like an assembly line. FOLLOW-UP That night there was slight discomfort for a couple of hours.You have to keep your eyes closed for the day. Day two I could see pretty well & I had my follow-up appointment with Dr. Wang, which was a joke. He's so sweet, but the whole visit consisted of waiting for him, a quick look at my eyes, & then a marketing recruitment. "Post this pic on Facebook, write a review here & write one here." Not going to lie, this freaks me out! I want honest reviews, not forced reviews written by half-blind recovering LASIK patients that feel obligated because they were put on a time crunch to write a review before leaving the office. 6 MONTHS LATER: My eyes took forever to heal. They were dry & I feared they would be like that forever. It wasn't until month 3 that I noticed my life might not consist of eye drops every hour. But, they didn't actually heal for 6 months! My advice to others is to remember that you may wake up & be fine the next day, but it may take 3-6 months. Be prepared for that, don't get discouraged if this happens to you. Tips: Take fish oil pills, get a humidifier, & get the surgery done in the summer. They didn't tell me until AFTER my surgery that those that have surgery in the winter usually suffer dry eye more.

However, the biggest problem was that the dining room was too noisy to carry on conversation. Maybe it's that way most of the time, but that night there was an extremely loud table of eight. text: I have literally been thinking about coming here for almost twenty years (or however it has been open) and for some reason or another, just haven't gotten around to it. Finally did so...And the following is my report. A very good fish restaurant doing some nice unfussy food that overall is well performed. I had four oysters with mignonette that was a little overpowering. I think I would have simply preferred them with a touch of lemon or perhaps dial back the vinegar (or again use a very light acidity rice-wine vinegar). Anyway, the oysters themselves were pristine and beautifully cared for. My wife had the red snapper ceviche which she liked. Then, a very nicely done piece of barely seared big-eye for my wife. Quite beautifully prepared even if the dish was a little busy. At some point it does become hard to figure where the main ingredient fits in. But huge kudos for one aspect of their food: it is incredibly light. There wasn't a single dish that relied on oil, butter, or other fats as its principle source of flavor and I can't tell you how happy that makes me. It was an entirely digestible, clean flavored meal. I had two apps instead of the main course (which inspired me a little less). So a beautiful plate of grilled octopus that was nicely balanced by little potatoes, pieces of beet, and various other little goodies that really made this a warm salad. Really well done. I love octopus and I really loved this plate. The other plate was perhaps the weakest of the dinner. A piece of Spanish Mackerel, a favorite fish of mine--to both catch and eat--which had been cooked "a l'unilatéral" (i.e. skin side down until it is essentially cooked through and the skin is crispy). A couple of things went wrong with this dish. It was very small: which was a little odd next to the octopus dish which was huge. In other words, the portion sizes are kind of all over the map. I don't know that I would have thought is was so small had the other app literally not been eight times bigger. Since I got both at the same time (more on that later) it just didn't look right. So this nice piece of mackerel had been cook on the skin. The problem was a)it had been cooked at too high a heat so the skin was burned. It's a delicate balance to get that skin just right, and they didn't hit it. Flame was too high--though I understand they wanted a little char. But there was too much. The other thing, and this was the big mistake, is that they flopped something on top of the fish (I'm writing this a few days later and I can't remember what it was) which immediately made the skin soft. So all that work getting the skin crispy was for naught. Instead, it was gummy. Which of course is exactly what you are trying to avoid. I told the kitchen about it and was a little surprised that they didn't appear more interested in hearing about my experience with their food. I had been listening to that shop talk during our meal so I know they care about food and its prep. But does that mean that you should ignore a customer who, believe it or not, and contrary to most, actually knows what he's talking about? Believe me boys, I've been working with fish longer than some of you have been alive. So why not listen? Can't hurt, right. I know most people don't know squat. But I'm not one of them. OK. So the service was a little surprising, particularly given a virtually empty restaurant. The woman serving was nice enough when we walked in. Somewhat aloof but passably gracious. Throughout the meal, she remained mostly on top of things. Not too present, kept our glasses filled but didn't ask us how we were doing every three minutes (which I hate). So far so good. What was less good was giving me both my apps next to each other when one was supposed to be the app and the other the main course. It looked ridiculous and it was impossible to eat that way. Why not just fire one after the other and serve them in sequence? It's not like either dish was going to take that long--especially not the mackerel. At least ask me how I want them served if you have any doubts. It just didn't make any sense and it was inelegant. But that was relatively minor. What was far less comprehensible was the fact that once we had finished our meal, left a generous 25% tip and gone for our coats, she didn't bother to bid us good evening or anything. She saw us get up and never bothered to turn around or anything. It's a couple of words, but it is the most basic of things. So instead of leaving on a high note, we were thinking WTF was her problem there? And indeed, what was the problem? We had been soft-spoken, enjoyed a good meal, and were feeling very good about the place. And then boom, a sense that as soon as the money had been forked over, the interest was gone. For a place that was 1/4 on a Thursday night, you'd have thought they would be more enthusiastic about keeping (a first-time!) customer happy. Guess not. Too bad. I may or may not come back for that reason.

text: I've been to Pinewood Social now for two very different occasions: drinks and happy hour with a group of lovely ladies and also casual lunch date in the middle of a workday. Both times I ended in supreme "eh." How dare I go state that a place built on being a bowling alley slash library slash coffee shop slash meeting room slash soon to open pool area formed on the basis of being THE socializing venue come away forgettable? The food. The food here is like they found an awesome menu abandoned by one of the original and tasty restaurant ventures nearby and tried to recreate the dishes, forgetting seasoning, freshness, heat lamps...the basics. The menu is so unoriginal I want to cry at the way it's shoddily built up over the solemn headstones of our Nashville standard pork rinds and Sriracha and cauliflower and goat's cheese...all tossed out without a blip of original extra flavor adds or creative mash up. The entire place talks like a pinterest dreamer's idea of how every bit of the coolest 36 restaurants from 36 various places around the world should be thrown together into what should become the cumulative of coolness but ultimately reveals that's seeing a slick-lit porn-tastic print of cleverly topped crostinis and "pinning" that to your menu only means you've got a good eye - not a good grasp on your kitchen. Plus wise the servers and bar tenders here are incredibly nice. I'm not sure if they're getting lost between bowling and kitchen though because they're also pretty slow. My mascarpone and my chevre and so on sounded delicious but they came out on pre-crisped bread now cold and texture-dead, tasting more or less like the lackluster airplane food cousin version of the yum - sounding ingredients they boasted. My veggie Bahn mi had great bread and a thin smattering of plain veggies in the roll. A few bites in, the things went soggy and cold before I could finish. The sriracha was just sriracha and when I asked for bbq sauce they had none...yet they have brisket on this menu!! Sinners! The lamb bolognese sauce was pretty standard but needed some herb to freshen up. We didnt get halfway through the pork rinds. They just kind of were dry, seasoning tossed on top like an afterthought if class...sucked. Overall, the repeatedly soggy cold breads leave me disenchanted with the kitchen feeling like they prep once in the morning and the flavor goes downhill from there. You can try to be all the things, but I really wanted at least a good restaurant here.

text: Good: A beautiful space, located in an up-and-coming area you wouldn't have wanted to visit 3 years ago. You walk in and immediately feel at home. The whole club, from bar area to bathrooms to the showroom, is intimate without being cloying. It fills a huge gap in this city, which has needed an upscale club inbetween tiny 75-100 seaters (eg Bluebird Café) and larger halls (Ryman). Very clean, great bathrooms, nice bar area. Lots and lots of wood. They're making their own wine next year, and the gigantic barrels are eye candy if you like good vino. The wine lists (there are 2) are comprehensive. Some very reasonably priced , but that's because they charge YOU the liquor tax. Be forewarned. Food is better than expected. Risotto balls, recommended by our waitress, were excellent (though I'd go for spicier mustard). Pork tacos ditto. The steak was two lovely pieces of meat - though the chef has a heavy salt hand. (Maybe they're salting and letting it sit to tenderize? Still, it shouldn't be that salty.) I don't recommend the mussels, and the cheese tray is absurdly small for what you pay, but the ravioli was gorgeous. The burgers are very good, and there's a vegetarian option too. I'd recommend the meze platter, except that we had it our first visit (opening night) and it was large enough for four. Last visit it had shrunk considerably. The bad: Five dollar parking charge? Really? The attendants make it clear that your $5 goes to the venue, so you're expected to tip on top of it. But there's NO street parking!! Getting seated is a work in progress. I've been here 5 times so far, alone, with family, with business associates. Each time, we arrived at 6 pm, when they opened. Each time, wait staff weren't ready. Each time, there's a meaningless cluster of hosts and hostesses? standing by the entry doors, doing anything but paying attention to the customers. Each time we were sent to the "concierge" for tickets and information. Forgive my being snotty about it, but how many City Winery employees does it take to seat someone? If it happened once, all right. But every time? Food service is slooooow. Don't come hungry. I don't know if the wait staff are over-loaded or what, but when you go out for an expensive evening like this, you expect better service. My waitrons have all been nice, but far from the kind of competency I experienced at the NY or Chicago clubs. Food is expensive for what you get. (Online menu prices changed?) Our party of four had a bottle of inexpensive wine, 3 Tito's vodkas, and two beers, plus mains and 2 appetizers) was $310 before tip. I think that's expensive. Portions aren't big enough for leftovers. If this were The Palm, I'd expect it, and I'd be satisfied knowing the quality would be wonderful AND I'd have enough for another meal next day. The wait staff are friendly, but scattered. Ask for salt and pepper. Ask again. And again. Finally ask a bus boy, who brings it eventually. My wife's burger arrived with fries, everything looked great, but by the time salt and ketchup arrived everything was cold. This is not unusual here, but I can no longer excuse it as growing pains. And they don't pay the liquor tax?!?! This is the only restaurant in Nashville charging the customers for it - even Kayne Prime, home of 50 cent charge per blue cheese olive in your drink, doesn't charge liquor tax. Really, between food prices and liquor tax, I would not suggest eating here. The ugly: Sound problems. It carooms off the back wall so you can't hear vocals at all if there's a band - of the 3 we've seen, this was a problem with all of them. It's all right for an acoustic act like Taj Mahal, but something needs to be done. Who opens a club in Nashville without consulting a sound engineer? Everyone in my party, each time, was disappointed in the sound quality. Seating is, to put it bluntly, horrendous. At first glance, it's very pretty - until you realize that a) no matter where you sit, you're not facing the stage, and b) chairs are tiny, and tables are about a foot shy of the standard 2 or 4 seat table length. What this means is that no matter how much you pay, or what you reserve, you're going to be miserably uncomfortable. My wife is petite, our daughter is likewise, but even they complained that they couldn't eat without elbowing one another. The sideways-only seating means you don't get to enjoy the show the way you would with concert-style. I understand you can't do the concert-style and serve dinners, but I'd love to see this place change up so half the table is facing the stage. The other half could just turn their chairs around for the show. As it is, no one was happy with the seats. All in all, I will continue to attend when I'm in town, because they're bringing in a lot of acts you wouldn't normally see in Nashville. But I'll dine elsewhere. And I'll try to get validated, even if I'm not a "vinofile" (because I resent paying $75 a year for what I would get), and I'll avoid ordering liquor.

text: As a three year tenant of The Preserve, I feel rather qualified to at least leave an opinion on the conditions of the apartment. The location is also very convenient to Brentwood and downtown Nashville. I'll start with the worst issue that we had while living here. text: The infamous La Colombe, Frankford Ave...I want to give this barn like palace five stars but I just can't. Let's talk about the good stuff first... The artsy Fishtown location feels dominating and towering inside, like a large night club, but guess what? It works phenomenally for coffee and spirits! It's a breath of fresh air, compared to the average miniature coffee shop. After eating a chocolate chip muffin I decided to rob the place. I went to the counter and said, "Put all the pastries in my bag", "and put whatever doesn't fit, in your organic cardboard boxes". They stared. I frowned. Back to my seat. Yes, they are that good. I'm always impressed by the coffee selections, they live up to the unique descriptions. The fact that you can also get coffee been brewed beer adds a bit of fun and creativity to the menu. Feel free to skate around this palace and gauk at shiney espresso machines and beefy beer distillation machines... fancy-shmancy glam. You will find yourself surrounded by gigantic wooden doors, and bakers-a-bakin, I feel like I'm watching an Amish farm operate sometimes. It's very interesting. So far, so gooood... but then, disaster strikes.... LA COLOMBE HATES WHIPPED CREAM... They don't have this heavenly coffee balancing foam anywhere in the vaccinity. I thought to myself, are they a cult? What's going on!? I had to double check my surroundings, as I tripped over a little bit, I had to make sure I wasn't accidentally inducted in. I almost cried when I discovered this. I begged them for an alternative. Creme fresh? I don't know.. You can't mess with one of the best things to happen to my mouth since, ever. You might be the new coffee mob boss on the block, Godfather Colombe, but you can't mess with the Diety of the whipped! You're a whipped cream athiest. But I still accept you.. Ok, so I'll forgive you (cringing) for that. But should I get over the fact that your baristas seem like they are best friends Juno? I'm not the only one who feels like this btw. Every time I visit I feel like I'm being taken care of by a mr. or mrs. hipster neutrality. I noticed some batistas smile, but no one seems that cheerful. Maybe they need some whipped cream? But overall all the workers seem cool and smart! The waiters are the nicest of the bunch. The solution for more smiles= whipped cream. The seating looks great, and most of it is designed comfortably (even though you will only find solid wood for your tush..) but I miss a comfy couch or chair to study on. Comfort is half the reason I visit a coffee shop. It's still here. The rocking chair area is very comfy. Just no padding for the tush... The Amish nod. Did the owner grow up sleeping on a wooden bed? Honestly La Colombe is half in the 3 star zone, but makes up for it by going overboard into the 5 star zone, with great coffee and more. So that puts us at 4 stars. It's a mixed feeling kind of place, a fancy palace to take your out of town friends. It's already filled with touristy flockers. It's exciting but different. Thanks for the great coffee.

text: TheDailyMeal.com recently posted an article on 101 Best Restaurants in America for 2015; Galatoire was ranked #22..... I've only come to New Orleans for work, so dining on my "to eat" lists are rare as I'm in back to back meetings, and often with others that do not necessarily have the same palette as I do. As you can imagine, I was thrilled to be able to convince a few colleagues of mine to check out Galatoire for dinner! Sure this place looks old school classy; imagine checked floors, waiters that invented what customer service looked like, and a suit jacket for all men during dinner service. Old school without the snobbishness factor.. I liked it! The food, let's just get straight to the point.. how was it you ask? -Galatoire Goute: A sampler of shrimp remoulade, crawfish, and crab. All three were dressed in a thick and creamy sauce.. imagine an overly sauced chicken salad but replace with Cajun/southern seasonings and replace protein with each respective seafood. I was starving so the crab worked, especially with a nice chuck of crusty bread. Shrimp's remoulade sauce was more of a creamy cocktail sauce that was unappetizing; the crawfish coated thickly was overly seasoned and remained on the plate unfinished. Of the three items, the crab was the most worthy, but that is already giving too much credit. -Lemon Fish: two colleagues ordered this, one topped with a lemon butter sauce and the other the same way but also topped with almonds. The fish was pan seared and cooked perfectly. Topped with a mild butter sauce and a nice squeeze of lemon to have the acid cut right through the thickness. A good fish if you're looking to steer away from the sauces, but nothing special about this entree. -Crawfish Etouffe: I expected more POW! More ZING! More FLAVOR BOMBS! Instead I got a consistency that was a touch thicker than broth, chunks of crawfish mixed with some stewed veggies, over rice. Not an expert on this dish, but I was indifferent about the flavors; nothing wow'd me but wasn't horrible either. Definitely not crave worthy Crab Yvonne: A sautee of lump crab meat, mushrooms, green onions, artichoke hearts, and a light butter lemon sauce. Add a squeeze of some extra lemon and enjoy! This was definitely one of the better dishes of the night! Turtle Soup: Not sure why I envisioned this to be a broth based soup, but was surprised when it came out and upon delivery it was more of a roux concoction. Deep flavor, and a bit salty after eating a few bites. Heavy and hearty, but very similar flavors to gumbo minus the rice. Good, but not great. Bread Pudding: Really, Yelpers?! As a highlighted thing to get, I have to SMH at you guys... it was a less cinnamony version of a cinnamon roll... aka just a chuck of baked dough with a thin praline sauce and a few slices of bananas. Sure, I like warm dough.. you got me.. and Yes I did eat it.. but was it worth the calories? Was it crave-worthy?! Absolutely not.. in fact.. a cinnabon sounds better at the moment! Overall, my taste buds were highly disappointed with my adventure here. #22 on the list in the WHOLE US of A in 2015? Bump it way down, TheDailyMeal.com, because you sir/mam are no longer a credible source for me.

text: Let me start by saying that I had been wanting to try Catch Twenty Three since my wife and I moved to Tampa. After nearly a year here we finally buckled down and went. My parents were in town so they came along. After sitting down we were greeted by our waiter, who was timely and polite for the most part, and we ordered our drinks, which came out fairly quickly. My mother, who ordered a pomegranate margarita, got nothing more than a glass of colored lime juice. No real flavor to the drink at all and incredibly sour. We also ordered the Oysters Rockefeller as an appetizer. Again, it came out fairly quickly. The oysters weren't bad, not great, but not bad. They were properly cleaned and seasoned well. For our entrées my wife ordered the Steak Diane, my mother the Filet Mignon, my father the Catch Salad with Shrimp and Mussels, and I ordered the Mixed Grill. Let me just say that the food was mediocre at best. My wife loved the sauce over her steak but the steak itself was under seasoned. They did a great job, however, cooking the meats to our preferred doneness. My mother had no complaints about the Filet Mignon but didn't really have any praise for it either. My father, on the other hand, didn't care for his pasta dish. Said it was incredibly bland. The shrimp were rubbery and chewy from being severely overcooked. The mussels were just cold and tasteless. Finally, the Mixed Grill I had ordered started off promising. It comes with chicken, steak, and pork. The steak was seasoned and cooked very well. The chicken was primarily seasoned with aromatic seasoning, so not a lot of, "in your face", flavor. The chicken was also cooked perfectly. It has the right tenderness to it and it was very juicy. The pork is where it starts to get scary. The meat was horribly undercooked to the point it was almost raw in the center. Needless to say I didn't eat much of that. From what I did taste in my first bite, though, the pork had been seasoned slightly and covered in sauce. This place seems to use their sauces to hide the fact that their food isn't worth the hefty prices they charge. My father has been sick for the last three days after our dinner here. He's been vomiting and has had moderate diarrhea. My wife had diarrhea the rest of the night after dinner but felt fine the next day. Luckily, my mother and I were spared from any would-be illnesses that could've come from Catch Twenty Three. Overall, the food, that of it that wasn't under or over cooked, was mediocre at best. The drinks were poorly put together and tasted awful. The staff was polite and timely with our food, but at what cost? I won't be going back to Catch Twenty Three. I give this a 1 out of 5 rating. Their only saving grace was the fact that they cooked most of the meats to our specified doneness and the fact that we're still alive. Sick as hell, some of us, but alive.

text: I've wanted to go to Mariachi's for quite a while and was excited to finally be able to go. The restaurant claims it serves authentic Mexican food, which I love. I've had the good fortune to visit Mexico many times and I was hoping to get that experience closer to home. Unfortunately I was less than impressed. The interior decor is dated and cosmetically in need of an update, but I've been to enough hole in the walls to know the food is what makes the place. The menu is expansive, which is a plus. The problem is that the food I had wasn't good. We were greeted immediately upon entering and sat down quickly. A waitress took our drink orders right away and brought chips with salsa verde. The chips were ok but the salsa verde was tasteless with the consistency of water. I ordered a side of guacamole to go with the chips. The guacamole was fresh and had a nice taste. We ordered combo fajitas, chicken chimichangas, and a side of refried beans. Our food was served within a decent amount of time, but we were not given silverware or napkins and there was no plate for the fajitas - we had to ask for all of it. The fajitas were bland, with no seasoning whatsoever. The steak was crunchy and the peppers were mushy with an acidic aftertaste. The chimichanga was ordered with mole sauce. The mole sauce tasted like thick old coffee and completely covered and saturated the chimichanga. The menus said it would be topped with onions and sour cream. There were no onions and I had to ask for sour cream. The chimichanga itself was bland, lacking in seasoning and flavor. I love authentic refried beans, which is why I ordered them as a side. They tasted as if they came from a can, the consistency was off and like everything else the beans lacked in seasoning and flavor. I am really disappointed. I was really hoping that this could be my new local go-to for a yummy authentic Mexican meal. Unfortunately I'll need to keep looking.

text: For five years, I have been waiting for this city to have a true creperie, a true French restaurant with buckwheat galettes with a side of simple greens that I could enjoy with a glass of wine. The restaurant is a quaint little place right on the edge of Mass Ave with a classic red and black theme that probably caters more to what Americans think of France, but is 100% adorable. There is a small bar to get wine, beer, cocktails, or coffee, and several small tables with a tiny lounge area next to a fireplace. And, true to French restaurant life, you get a fleeting glimpse of what's going on in the kitchen. They have an excellent wine selection as well as some cider and champagne. Highly recommend the "Mimi" with your galettes! About those galettes...mon dieu. Perfection. They are buckwheat crepes with savory ingredients inside. So, they are naturally gluten-free, and they have a few vegetarian options. I had the galette complete--a classic with ham, Gruyere, and egg. It tasted just like I remember when I lived in Nantes. My friend got the mushroom and cheese galette that has an amazing buttery texture. Couldn't ask for more. As for dessert, how could I not go for the classic buerre sucre crepe? Just butter and sugar, and it was perfect. No exaggerating. We also had a raspberry and lemon crepe at the table with a great balance of flavors. The lemon wasn't overpowering or too sweet. It was just right. And what can I say about the service? Everyone, and I mean everyone, was so nice and helpful. Shout out to Matt, our server, who was just as excited as we were about the food. The manager, Nicola, came by to tell us a bit about the restaurant and the food and seasonal menus that are coming up and took the time to let us know the hours. Obviously she could tell we will be regulars. And I even got to meet the owner and spout off some French with her. It was an enchanting dining experience, and I can't wait to go back for more. Take me back to France, Cropichon et Bidibule. We are going to be good friends.

text: I turned 40 not too long ago and have been enjoying the "Tex-Mex" food here at this particular Carmelita's since high school. Most outside of the Southwest US, were never exposed to real Mex until a few years ago. Besides, authentic Mex is now available at many other joints. If this is what you seek, you should have taken the trendy BUS? Carmelita's is our local "KING" of the Americanized Tex-Mex food you grew up with. I only subtract the 1 star for sloppy management that resulted in that lame news story. As for their menu stand-outs? Just their simple refried beans beat the sombreros and serapes right off of ALL the other "authentic" Mex joints in our area. Seriously! BUS Who? Plus sometimes, I really enjoy simple "gringo" tacos from my youth. Almost like I make at home, meaning a CRISPY corn tortilla shell, ground beef, and lettuce/tomato/cheese. Carmelita's are the very best in our area, and I've sampled many. Carmelita's also has great shredded pork tamales if you care for more traditional Mex fare. It's just simple shredded beef, slow simmered in a complex sauce, served over rice with tortillas on the side. Sure, everyone makes mistakes. There is a reason this joint has survived so many years, and has spawned so many other locations... It's because they put out the best TEX-MEX in our area...

Their menu of salads, soups, and salads is not an extensive one, but it has a little bit of something for everyone. On this day, I had the Baguette du Fromage, which is Gruyere and goat's cheese sandwiched between a whole wheat baguette with sliced tomatoes and mixed greens. Sandwiches are served with your choice of a mixed salad, potato salad or soup (tomato basil, miso, and crawfish bisque were the options). If they ran out of the soup, that tells me that it's good and gives me a reason to go back already. The sandwich was creamy, gooey deliciousness! The salad was also a nice mix of spring greens, carrots, cherry tomatoes and cucumber with a vinagrette dressing served separately. For $9, it was a very generous plate of food...very, very GOOD food! My friend order the rotisserie chicken club sandwich with potato salad. The sandwich had HUGE hunks of chicken on it to the point that it was falling out of the sandwich! It's great knowing that there's a quick and good lunch spot in Algiers that is within minutes of both home and the office. If you think you have to travel to the Eastbank to find a cute, comfy cafe with great food and a cool vibe, then you need to stop by Tout de Suite!

text: My first visit to Philadelphia came along with a craving for some good sushi. After a long day of doing typical center-city Philly touring, I finally got my boyfriend to agree to try sushi for the first time. He is the pickiest of picky eaters (both by personal preference and because of allergies), so I knew I needed to pick a really good place. Trusting my always faithful Yelp! app, I found Bleu. Granted, it wasn't my first choice (the place I wanted to go to had a gap between lunch and dinner), but it was held in high regards. Fellow Yelpers seemed to rave about this place, so I thought it was worth a try considering the circumstances. We walked here from the Independence Hall Center, and it took us about 15 minutes. The outside of the building isn't too much to rave about, considering we almost missed it. It is, however a blue door, with blue-framed windows and small sign that reads Bleu. Go figure. We walked in to a completely empty restaurant. Its a really small place, pretty much just a strip of booths and a center walkway with the actual sushi making station at the back. We were asked if we had a reservation, which seemed odd because the place was completely empty with the exception of the staff. We informed the server wearing Nike sweatpants and a blue t-shirt that we did not, but we were seated immediately anyway. I was quite confused throughout the entire meal service. You have a very trendy, upscale looking restaurant that lives up to the name of Bleu (because literally everything inside is a blue color), yet you have servers and employees that are half dressed in sweatpants and a t-shirt yet the other half wearing slacks and a black button down shirt? I didn't know if we were underdressed or just fitting in? Ok.. Anyhow, we took a look at the menu, and their prices are typical of sushi joints of the same caliber. Please keep in mind that sodas are served by the can! Prices are around $5-$6 for regular rolls, $4-$5 for nigiri, and $10-$15 for specialty rolls. Being the picky eater he is, my boyfriend ordered the teriyaki chicken ($13) as a fallback and I decided for us to share the Rittenhouse roll, the traditional Philly roll (when in Rome), and the Ten Street roll. The Philly roll was the most unedible of them all. It was mainly just mealy and mushy cucumber wrapped into a roll with a teeny bit of salmon and cream cheese. The cucumber was unpleasantly overbearing and left a funny taste in your mouth. Unfortunately, it was the first item my boyfriend tasted, and it made him weary to try anything else. I convinced him to try the rest. The Rittenhouse Square roll was okay at best. It would have been much better if the sprinkling of herbs/seasoning on top was omitted from the recipe. It was honestly a clash of flavors and made the roll taste awkward and out of place. The Town roll was the one that we both enjoyed the most out of the three. Don't be fooled. Just because we liked it the most out of the three doesn't mean it was actually good. It was the most edible. It seemed just like Albacore tuna from a can was dried out, put into a roll and deep fried. Slap some spicy mayo on top and you've just made yourself the Town roll. It was very crunchy, even for a deep-fried roll (almost like the consistency of a Dorito), and was difficult to chew. Service was nearly nonexistent. The only time they really came to check on us was once when my water glass was refilled. At the end of the meal service they brought us two complimentary ice cream samples. They were about the size of a tablespoon each and were a vanilla/peanut butter mixture- very odd for a sushi place to be offering peanut butter ice cream after a meal service? Anyhow, the bill came out to around $51 dollars, and after tip it it was close to around $65. In my personal opinion, this is a very hefty price to pay for sub-par sushi and non existent service. Lesson learned I guess. I'm almost embarrassed that I brought my boyfriend there for his first sushi experience, because it was that un-enjoyable. I'm from the Phoenix, AZ area where sushi is known to be less than favorable, and I have had better from some places in my neighborhood.

text: I had a wonderful meal at Mariza last night, shared with several coworkers. What a great experience! Kudos to Isaiah, who was our top notch server for the evening (and, as I found out, a neighbor as well!) I can't wait to go back! The atmosphere is contemporary, dark, and not at all loud or overcrowded. It was rainy outside, and though we Uber'ed ourselves to the restaurant, there was ample parking outside which is unusually nice. After our first bottle of wine, we started with the burrata crostini, whose delectable first creamy bite can only compared to the heavenly moment of cutting into a perfectly poached egg. Next up was the tuna (also on crostini), which was plated beautifully. Every bite was delicious - and I'm not someone who would typically order tuna-on-anything. I paired this with a Julia's Cup cocktail - worth every cent. I enjoyed the arugula salad with pickled vegetables, topped with ricotta - enough to have a little bit of cheese with every bite. The beets were a delicious touch to this salad, though the ricotta was definitely the star of the show. I also tasted the bresaola and crispy guanciale salads - both were fantastic. I'm not sure which of the three was the winner in this category, because they're all so different. What became clear very quickly is that the chef is very conscious of textures as well as flavors, and that put a smile on everyone's faces as we made our way through the menu. My entree was the black linguini with crab and shrimp, the larger size. It was delicious and plenty to share. The short rib rigatoni had flavors reminiscent of Grandma's beef stew. It was very rich. I also tried the hangar steak (fantastic), and the crispy layers in the vegetable lasagna reminded of a meal of crespelles I made with my partner in our little temporary apartment in Rome a few years back. One bite brought me right back to that moment in a way nothing else had since I left. A few bottles of wine later, we finished with one of each dessert for the table: chocolate terrine with sea salt, grapefruit sorbet, and apple/pear panna cotta. All three were wonderful and completely unique to each other, though the panna cotta was by far my favorite. While I realize meals like this are largely a success [or not] depending on whoever sits at your table, and I was lucky to share this meal with some wonderful people, the staff and atmosphere at Mariza enhanced everything about our experience. This is one of those restaurants that exists almost in my back yard, and I'd never stepped in until now. I'm really looking forward to returning. In a city with as many restaurants as there are diners willing to eat in them, Mariza gets it right.

text: Sampan has been on my "To Try" list for years - yes, literally years - and I finally made it there yesterday for Happy Hour. Why did it take me so long to make this dream come true, you ask? I was determined to take advantage of the great HH deals (which are seriously awesome) but they are only offered at the bar...and the bar is small...like really small...and was full at all my other attempts. But yesterday, the BF and I snagged two magical seats right after work, and it was definitely worth the wait. The HH drink specials are one house red wine, one house white wine, one 12 oz. pour of a beer on draft, and one specialty cocktail, each for $4, and then a bunch of small plates/appetizers that are all in the $4 - $7 range. It's a great deal for delicious food, and I was actually surprised at how big the "small plates" were. My HH "snack" ended up keeping me full enough that I didn't need to eat dinner. To eat, we had the kobe beef slides, the brusses sprouts and the mushroom dumplings. I don't eat meat, but the sliders were really cute looking (because, like, that matters in food) and my BF loved them. He likes his meat rare, and these were almost still mooing, so he was happy. On to the sprouts - holy lord they are awesome. First, the serving is a huge bowl. Second, the flavor is amazing - kind of like roasted meets Asian meets crispy. Just so good. And third - they were $4! The dumplings were also really good; four little fried pockets of mushrooms sitting in some broth with little pickled mushrooms (sounds weird, but totally works) and some foam on top. Small but tasty. Drinkwise, my man had the house red wine and I had the specialty cocktail, which was tequila and limeade - it was fine, not very strong and not the best thing I've ever had, but a good deal. All in all, our bill for the food and five drinks (it was a good day!) came to not even 35 bucks, which is a total steal. I'm docking one star because of a limited beer selection (there are only four options on tap, which just seems skimpy to me) and just a microscopic bar area - but if you can stalk your way to a seat, Sampan is totally worth it!

text: Burgers are my favorite "bad" meal - the kind of thing I crave when hungover or when I haven't eaten all day and want to get all my calories at one sitting. I have been to FLIP in Birmingham so I was eagerly anticipating the opening of this place here. Plus, I am a total Top Chef junkie and cannot resist a restaurant by someone I have seen on the show. So I was invited to the friends and family soft opening and agreed immediately. We got there and were seated immediately. Ambiance is casual but modern and slick and new. Big bar in the middle of the room and tables all around. If you were wondering about the menu, well, they have all types of burgers. Yes, as the name says, it is all about burgers so if you don't like that you probably shouldn't go. They do have a turkey burger option, some standard burgers, lamb burger, "chorizo" burger, etc and so forth. And they have sides such as fries cooked in beef fat (um...YESSSS), onion rings, etc. Oh and they also have booze, which is my favorite. Drinks were good cocktail creations and there were choices for whatever liquor you prefer. They also have beer and such. And probably Coke and water too but...boring. Given my first trip to FLIP in Birmingham I steered away from the chorizo burger. Not that it isn't good, but that it isn't CHORIZO. To me, that implies a burger either mixed with or totally made out of CHORIZO which is SAUSAGE. This is PORK with CHORIZO SPICES. There's a big difference. Just FYI. So this time I went with the lamb burger because I can totally get into any Mediterranean flavors. The burger was big and well spiced and flavorful. The fries were good as only fries cooked in beef fat can be...if they were just a smidgen skinnier I'd be putting these on my best French Fries list. Service was friendly and excited if a bit disjointed but it was a soft opening so overall was impressed. Our waitress was so pumped about everything on the menu and seemed excited to be working there so it was really fun and refreshing. Definitely give this place a try when you are craving a burger. I know I will since it is not too far from my house and there are so many other burgers to try on the menu!

text: I bought the Living Social deal for The Library specifically because I wanted to try the Prime Rib. I love Prime Rib and have been on a hunt for the best Prime Rib in Indy. My current favorite is Bynum's, and after dining at The Library...my current favorite is still Bynum's. My Husband and I had 7:30pm reservations, which I was glad I made because there were several people in the restaurant lobby waiting for a table. We were seated promptly. I liked the waitress and the art filled interior of The Library was nice, though it made me curious as to the name of the restaurant since there was nary a book nor anything else library-like in site. Now back to the Prime Rib,... Upon placing my order shortly after 7:30pm (with much anticipation I might add) for a 12 oz. medium-rare slice of goodness, I was informed that only medium and above choices were available. My face fell, quite visibly I'm sure. This was not anticipated since it was still so early in the evening. Since I had been looking forward to Prime Rib ALL DAY and it was the reason we were there, I went ahead and ordered the most rare medium they had. "Out of medium rare this early, REALLY?" I said to my Husband after the waitress walked away. (He wisely opted for the New York strip. Medium rare, of course. I suspect if I had been a "medium well" girl we wouldn't have made it past the first few dates.) When our meals arrived, I sliced into my Prime Rib, gamely giving it a try, very much wanting to like it. I didn't. It was plain. It was dry. It also wasn't medium, it was more next door to done I'd say. My plan was to eat it, because I was starving, the steak was there, and I didn't want to cause a ruckus. Combing the bites of steak with the mashed potatoes and rice pilaf I had ordered as sides, along with dunking each bite into the provided au jus, would get me by I thought. My Husband, sensing my disappointment, asked me about my meal though he already knew what my answer would be. He later told me he saw pain in my eyes. LOL. When the waitress stopped by, he spoke up first, saying what I felt bad about voicing out loud, and the waitress kindly and without a hint of irritation asked if I would like to order something else. I opted for the filet mignon, once again medium rare. I am happy to report that the filet, which was delivered in a reasonable amount of time later, was correctly cooked. (As was my Husband's New York strip, by the way, which I encouraged him to go ahead and finish while I waited for my replacement.). The taste though, was just okay, on the plain side. The same actually, can be said about the potatoes and rice pilaf I mentioned earlier. Not bad, but not like, "Wow, I can't wait to eat this again!" And not worth the $$ price of the The Library. Though he did not openly say so, I suspect my Husband felt the same was as he chose not to place either of his remaining sides (mashed potatoes and green beans) in our take home container. The best parts of the meal, I'd have to say, were the openers. The French Onion Soup (though I prefer Bynum's), the Cesar salad, and the bread. The bread especially was very good. Judging from the other Yelp reviews as well as the number of people dining there the night we went, The Library definitely has its fans. Perhaps we were there on an off night?

text: It was January 11th, 2003 when I first became introduced to Famous Dave's. It wasn't by way of their restaurant, but rather their BBQ sauce. The setting could not have been better, as a group of friends rallied together in FDR Park for an Eagles tailgate party. Fellow Yelper, Tom B. (VA) had brought a bottle of FD's Rich & Sassy BBQ sauce for our soon to be grilled chicken. The sauce was absolutely terrific! I ended up locating their product online and ordering some bottles for myself shortly thereafter. It remains my sauce of choice to this very day! By the way, the Eagles were victorious that night, as they went on to a 20-6 playoff romp over Michael Vick and his Atlanta Falcons on a bitter cold but joyous evening in South Philadelphia! To date, there are approximately 200 Famous Dave's nationwide. In the later half of the first decade of the new millennium Dave's started to infiltrate the Delaware Valley including their monster of a location in Springfield, PA (adjacent to the older Target and LA Fitness). I still recall the joy that I felt when the news had been broken. In addition to the great sauces, I have always found FD's to be a great destination when we have the kids in tow. The restaurant itself is neatly decorated with the plenty of eye catching animals (including Smokey the Bear), signs, a big fireplace, etc... The kids are also provided with coloring books and crayons upon being seated. Lil' Wilbur's menu offers 6 options all under $6 and include, drink, side, and Oreo cookies. Our kids love the chicken fingers. As indicated in my first paragraph, I love their sauce. To atart you out, FD's serves up a plate of their kettle chips, which provides the opportunity to sample a plethora of sauces that they have available. The Sweet & Zesty and Rich & Sassy are my favorites. Their sauces and seasonings are also available for purchase in the rear of the restaurant from their take-out section. I believe their sauces are also distributed through select grocery chains. FD's also provides full catering menu options for parties. The food is decent here. Famous Dave's claims to cook from scratch and to start the BBQ fresh around 4 a.m. or so every morning! I usually go for the ribs and the wife will opt for the Hickory Chicken sandwich. They also offer some great side dishes. My favorite is the sweet corn, which is seasonal. The fries are also very good, more like mini potato wedges, and provide another great opportunity to test out the sauces! I am fully in favor of getting "sauced" at Famous Dave's!

Then for my entree, I ordered something I could not pronounce (which is a shame since I work for a French company): Les crepes aux fruits de mer et aux epinards. I ordered the large portion which was a mistake because they gave me 2 stuffed crepes which were not small by any means. They were definitely a hit mostly because they were different and quite delightful to look at. The rhum balls were quite rich that if I was to eat 2, it would have been way too much. Lastly, the truffles were good but did not quite blow me away. In short, I have had better truffles. With that said, I would love to go back and try their creme brulee and some of their cake varities!

text: I love tacos in just about any shape and form, and there are so many street food style tacos in town that when a taco place pops up that goes beyond that, I've not only gone to heaven, but I've gone to heaven holding a taco in each hand. Corazon has done a great job to showing us that there's amazing tacos beyond the basic meat, cilantro, onion combination. Something, I suspect, I'd get to experience if I spent time in Mexico sampling its vast array of regional specialties. The owners have taken family recipes, added local, fresh and seasonal ingredients, and hit the taco jackpot. What you can expect includes a freshly made tortilla or tostada shell, a meat taco, several seafood and ceviche options, and a vegetarian taco made of ingredients inspired and sourced from the Saturday farmers market the day before. The salsas to accompany them are also wonderful, like pickled onions and garlic, pineapple habanero salsa, and a chile peanut arbol and you might find you've eaten before any of your order has arrived. I am in no way a vegetarian, but the majority of the time the market taco is my favorite of the day. The flavors and combinations are so damn good. But that doesn't mean that's all I get. It's really best to go to Corazon with a friend or two and order one of everything to share around. Pay with cash, or credit card - they have Square. You can also expect a long line, and a wait for your food to arrive because each dish, which is served a la carte, is assembled to order. Prices range from $4-6 for the tacos and are generally $10 for the ceviche tostadas. So: not street food prices for not street food tacos. Did I say there's a long line? Sometimes it is out the door, and sometimes they sell out of dishes within an hour or two of opening. It's that line that's proof of concept, because Santa Barbara is not used to lines and not used to paying much for tacos, yet they will do it for Corazon. Don't just take my word for it, go stand in the line yourself! You order at the counter, pay, get a number and find somewhere to sit. They will bring out the dishes, one per plate, as they become available. So sometimes you'll get them trickling over one at a time, sometimes they'll come all at once. Another good reason to share with a friend. The dishes can get a little messy, but they are so good, I have zero dignity about getting it all over my face, my hands, dripping down my arms. The stuff they serve here is by far the best tacos currently in Santa Barbara, the menu changes weekly and only available one day a week, Sundays...FOR NOW. Corazon is a pop-up operating out of Three Pickles Deli downtown, but will be moving to its own brick and mortar location hopefully later this year. In the meantime, coming here is getting to be a Sunday tradition. You can see the menu on their FB page, or instagram (@corazoncocinasb) usually by Saturday afternoon, after Chef Ramon has gone to the farmers market. ps. if you absolutely cannot handle waiting in that line, you are in luck that Corazon is on one of the tastiest food blocks in town to console yourself with. But you will have to watch all the post-Corazon diners stroll by looking pretty happy and full.
label: POS

text: Very good sushi, especially considering its location. I enjoyed BlueFin, and in fact, it's on the cusp of being great, but some missteps hold it back. BlueFin has some traditional elements, and two of the main sushi chefs are even Japanese! The interior is clean, swanky and bright, which somewhat belies the suburban-sprawl shopping center exterior. Service is attentive and pleasant, although not all staff is knowledgeable about the menu. I had the sushi omakase plus a hamachi kama (grilled yellowtail collar). I added a couple pieces for gluttony's sake. The head chef cut the fish, although he handed off the fish to an assistant for creating the nigiri. I was somewhat disappointed in this, since for some, the rice is the most important element. Not here. The assistant chef handed me the sushi plate, which was all presented at one time, even the hot anago (throws off the temperature!), and couldn't name all the pieces. That said, the fish was very fresh and interesting. Not terribly varied (i.e., I came in looking forward to toro and uni, both of which they did not have), although what they have is very good quality. Rice is nicely vinegared but a touch below room temperature. I could have used a little more pizazz. Nori (seaweed paper) is crisp and fresh, and the ginger and wasabi (yes!!) is fresh. This is a major step up from the fake stuff, horseradish, etc. you see elsewhere. Here's a more detailed rundown on what I had: - Miso soup - comes with the sushi omakase, large portion, but lacked real seaweed or even tofu, so I set it aside - Edamame - deliciously fresh and nicely salted. Again, large portion This is around the time that I noticed most of the sushi chefs are not Japanese and are basically churning out gross rolls. Forgive me for the disdain. - Omakase nigiri - 8 pieces of sushi. Again, the head chef selected and cut the fish, and then handed it off to an assistant to form the nigiri. They apply a touch of fresh wasabi under the fish, which is great and authentic, but then the plating was an absolute disaster. Not sure why they'd want all the fish cramped as such and touching each other. That disturbs the flavor, temperatures, and especially aesthetic appearance. Highlights were the hamachi (very fresh), engawa (with shiso leaf), scallop (nicely cut), and anago (fresh, not frozen). - Gluttony course - 2 pieces of ikura, very fresh (roe popped in my mouth), loved the seaweed paper, since it was crisp and delicate. The 2 pieces of tamago were made in house, which is a major plus. Delicious, eggy and sweet - Hamachi kama - Again, very fresh, and cooked nicely. Crisp exterior, juicy buttery, fatty interior. Served with house-made ponzu with scallions on the side, which is more sophisticated than the average Chinese-joint fronting as a Japanese restaurant. Sadly, there was no grated daikon radish, which is symbolic of the 4, not 5-star rating - Complementary fruit course - This was a nice touch, and very authentic. For some reason, Japanese restaurants never place much emphasis on dessert, which isn't a bad thing, since I like fruit. Fritter was a bit odd, but again, fits the slightly nuveau-ish aspect to BlueFin So, BlueFin masters the core of Japanese, but when they branch out, they don't branch out with exotic, yet authentic items (think uni, natto, tuna belly) but rather fusion dishes. This is not the worst thing in the world, as I get a sense that they purchase what is fresh and don't mess with lower quality fish.

It was also very flavorful and moist. I wish all scones could be this good. The rittenhouse square is also wonderful. It has an indulgent layer of caramel on top and some graham cracker crust and brownie stuff. This is a must try. Not to be forgotten, I eyed cookie sandwiches being prepared and I could not help but impulsively request one. I'm very glad I did. The chocolate chip cookies themselves were an excellent iteration and the cream inside was thick, sugary, and sweet. I cannot stop thinking about it. The sticky bun was also very good. text: This is my new favorite place for BBQ!!! It's been open for 10 years and I'm just now discovering it, thanks to a groupon my hubby bought. I had the rib sampler that came with rib tips and ribs, 2 sides, and a choice of bread. I had coleslaw and Mac n cheese for my sides and sweet corn muffin. My husband had the special of the day which was BBQ meatloaf with 2 sides and bread. You can choose from a small or large portion. He went with the small portion, green beans, ranch beans, and sweet corn muffin. To our surprise the mac n cheese, coleslaw, and ranch beans were beyond delicious and we ate our sides before eating the meats. That's especially rare for my husband since he's a carnivore lol green beans were good as well just not as good as the other sides we tried. Both the rib tips and ribs were tender and had loads of flavor, the portion size was big enough to take leftovers for lunch. Corn muffins were a delight, I don't like corn bread and I ate all of it, it was great! I loved it and will definitely be visiting frequently. My husband had nothing but praises about his food and he's a big meatloaf guy, so to find a place with delicious meatloaf and BBQ under one roof was like Rays of sunshine through a cloudy sky lol The service was great, the man at the register immediately acknowledged us, asked if it was our first time there, and made suggestions when we said yes. He pointed out the lunch menu and the special of the day. The man was friendly and had conversations with everyone in there. He brought our food to our table and even went to get us condiments from the self serve counter of condiments. The place was clean, smelled delicious, and welcoming. I wasn't sure if it was a tip type of place since it was a cafeteria type deal, but service was excellent so we tipped. You must try this place, you won't regret it!

text: A Cathedral of many names and many years. "Basilica of St. Louis, King of France." "Basilica St. Louis" or now "The Old Cathedral. Built from 1830 to 1835 it was the first Cathedral built west of the Mississippi. While many consider it to be on the Arch grounds it really sits on it own property. In the 1930's St. Louis wanted to build the Gateway Arch and took most of the land along the riverfront for the purpose of this monument. It was taken by eminent domain. Can't take a church by eminent domain hence it stood. While not a huge church nor ornate it has stood in St. Louis as the center of the Catholic Church. And the western part of the United States. What many need to understand the "Louisiana Purchase" took place in 1803. For this area was part of France. The United States was really an eastern conglomeration of old English colonies. This was the beginning of the formation of what is now the United States. And this Basilica was built a mere 27 years after the purchase. I hope the significance of this Cathedral is more understandable.

text: "Dude, what does my tattoo say?" ........ EVERY SINGLE TIME. But we finally made it. I came in a little late (12 minutes), to the chagrin of my family and friends who had already been there probably for a half an hour. Nancy is almost ALWAYS early. So I missed the ooooh and aaaah part that goes along with checking out the ambiance to a new restaurant. I still furtively checked it out as the meal progressed, but I just didn't get a good feel for the place. One thing I did notice, and should have asked about. Does anyone ever come here and actually watch the TV? More on that later.... So first off I order up a Negroni...it was pretty good. Not "amazeballs" as Dale might say, but it was pretty darn good. So I ordered another to sip through the rest of the meal. And Oh what a meal it was!! Everyone else ordered up something...steaks and fish and Kiwi even got a special spinach salad for picky eaters. I ordered up one of the fish specials for the evening. Halibut Moroccan. I had asked what the price was and was told it was $24. A little high for my normal wheel house, but this was a fancy cloth napkin night..so I splurged. I splurged more than I thought. When the bill came the charge was $32! Normally I would have been a LOT flustered and talked to someone and would have gotten all weird. Ok, more weird than normal. But I didn't. I just looked at the bill and said to myself. "Yep. Totally worth every single stinking penny." Especially when I was "gifted" Erica's leftovers. She is such a kind soul. Every single bit of this dish was perfection. Delicate and filling all at once. This is what I have always imagined great fish to be like when cooked. So how in the world could I complain on price when it was the best cooked fish I have ever eaten? I was also able to snag a little bite of Robert's pork chop before it left the table. It was cooked right and it was pretty good, but the breading was a little sweet. Sometimes my desire to have new experiences over rides my sense of decorum. I probably wont be allowed to sit next to Robert anymore. The apps were good but nothing that spoke to me personally. Then out came the Dessert Trio Sampler. I dove into the chocolate ones first. They were sooo good. But then.... And now we go back to my first question.."Does anybody actually watch the TVs?" my eyes rolled into the back of my head. I couldn't see a TV or hear anybody at my table or even feel the seat under my body. I had just taken a bite of that nondescript Baklava. I had not been expecting much. Instead I got much much much! My daughter even made note of it as I savored the bite. She implied I had a look of ecstatic euphoria and to be frank I did. Now don't let me oversell this item as some sort of magical talisman that will bring back your feelings of youthful days at that Poison concert. But instead, let me impart to you the momentary singularity of perfection in the balance of joy, contentment, friendship, alcohol, savory and sweet. I know I know...get back to the review... The service was as I expected from reading all the Yelp reviews and hearing my friends talk about it over and over....friendly and professional at the same time. Now the question begs....will I go back? Do I mess with that perfect memory? Or do I risk it to have a great meal with Ly'? I'm pretty sure if you know me, you know my answer on that one. (FTR that was 6 names dropped.)

text: Two words. Han Dynasty. This place is exactly like Han Dynasty but with some Taiwanese cuisine added on the menu. Supposedly...except I found the food here to be mediocre. What draws people in (at least what drew me in) is the hip trendy vibe the renovations of this establishment and the new-ness factor, but what brings them back should be the food. I don't think I would come back for the food. Minus the few authentic Sichuan cuisine items that people probably would not order, such as beef and tripe and tendon, there's really nothing authentic or special about the food in this restaurant. I don't know about you but there's no point for a Chinese person like me to go out and order mediocre Chinese food. Don't get me wrong, I'm not just talking about authenticity of my home country's cuisine. I love all Chinese food. There's authentic Chinese food (Sichuan, Hong Kong, Sanghai, Hunan, Yunnan, you name it..) and there's "fake" American Chinese food (like sesame chicken, kung po chicken, etc). I love them both because I love food. What I don't like is when mediocre food is sold off as some specicialized trendy cuisine with rip off prices. I feel like Dan Dan tries to do that. Some food I've tried for lunch with a coworker: 1. Lo mein with Taiwanese sausage--I love Taiwanese sausage and occasionally crave lo mein so I ordered this dish. The Taiwanese sausage protein choice costed $2 than the others (pork, chicken, beef, etc). I expected like a WHOLE sausage sliced up in my lo mein. Nope. It was probably like a few thin strands of what looked like ham and that was it. The rest was just noodles and a few thin slices of cabbage. The noodles themselves were way too salty. This was very terrible fake Chinese food. 2. Kung pao pork--Not spicy at all, no flavor at all. Kung pao pork is supposed to be spicy!! They were good cuts of pork but flavor was something left to be desired. They might as well just called it pork n veggie stir fry with ornamental chillis and peanuts. 3. Beef and Tripe in Chili Oil--This dish was hot hot hot and tasted very similar to that found at Han Dynasty. However, I believe Han Dynasty's tasted slightly better from what I remembered. 4. Rice--I judge chinese restaurants by their rice. The rice here was overcooked and mushy. Not the best rice imo but that's up to you to decide. Overall, the lunch menu was just ridiculous. Every lunch special entree sounded like the exact same thing. One choice of protien stir-fried with a vegetable and a soy-sauce based sauce. Chinese food should not be like this. There should be some thought that is put into the creation of the food! I don't go out to have you mass manufacture me a stir-fried salad in a wok with soy sauce. For that, there's better places like Honeygrow down the street. Only upside to this place is the atmosphere was nice and presentation of the food in general was very nice and pleasing to the eye. All the waitstaff were very friendly. The service was good and the decor was fun. Each table came with a cast iron tea pot, a caraffe of water, and bright orange coasters. On the flip side, I was dissappointed to find out that although the tea came in a fancy pot (like the sets you see in Teavana) the tea was just your plain old boring weak Chinese restaurant tea water. It wasn't even anything like oolong or jasimne. The decor is pretty much what you're paying for, that and the location in Center City. I suspect all the decor will get old and unappealing from wear and tear. I already saw this happening with their paper menus. They were dotted with specks of food and grease marks from patrons touching them over and over. I really think DanDan should consider regularly reprinting the menus so people don't lose their appetite from looking at the grime on them. The food is just really so-so and disappointing at a higher than normal price, too. There's really NO reason to eat this food in Rittenhouse when you can get this elsewhere in Chinatown for less than HALF the price. This place gives me the impression of trying too hard to be cool, when the food doesn't match the expectations set by the decor or the location. There's tons of better food in Rittenhouse that deserve the prices they charge. Perhaps I'll revisit and try something off the full menu just to be fair and give DanDan a second pass, but for now, I would say avoid for lunch.

Upon arrival, there were two of us who showed up early to provide the wait staff and hostesses a time to get a table ready and begin the wait (if there was one). The restaurant, on a Saturday evening at ~6:15pm, was nearly empty with some sections even being closed off for inactivity (and thus no wait). Right away they set up a table for us. We were however told that the majority of our party had to be there to be seated. While this normally wouldn't have been an issue, we were told to sit in the lobby area that was obviously were people came/left and when the doors opened, the sub-freezing temps (28°) didn't feel very nice to put it politely. At 7:00 pm, when everyone finally showed up, our waitress then took orders and forgot an entire person! 45 minutes later, she comes back and says "I just got your orders in". This was also the first drink refill time. Those that ordered appetizers and drinks did not see them until ~8:00. Around 8:30, she eventually returned for refills and we asked her to start bringing out food items as they were ready (piecemeal for our large party). Half of the orders came out completely cold, obviously having sat some time. 1-2 order began to trickle in over the next few minutes as they came up but this was still 1.5 hours later! Eventually 3 orders remained and 1 steak that was severely under-cooked, oozing red when it was supposed to be Medium-Well. By the time the steak was re-cooked, the young lady who ordered it was no longer hungry and gave away the properly cooked meat after already giving away the breaded shrimp that she had ordered grilled with her meal, as well. The last 3 items were a salad (A SALAD) and two burgers. When the burgers came out, they were both wrong. One was incorrectly a double and one had "garden" when it shouldn't. The salad, last of everything, was supposed to have chicken strips on it. They were barely warm. As this was supposed to be a brand new salad, there is no excuse for cold meat. This is now the 2 hour mark... One order, that did come out in reasonable time, was a steak and grilled shrimp entrée (much like the young lady before). The shrimp also came breaded. The waitress rudely told that person that his item doesn't come with grilled shrimp to which he begrudgingly said ok as he was too hungry at this point to complain. Later we learned that he had been ordering the same item WITH GRILLED SHRIMP for over 13 years at other TGIFs. The waitress came back and said a grilled shrimp order would be "dropped" for us. Around the 1:45 hour mark, a replacement shrimp order came that was STILL BREADED. It was returned. Around the 2:25 mark, as we were close to leaving, after the other 3 meals FINALLY made it, the grilled shrimp came out. The salad being the last item was unacceptable. We continued to speak up, hoping to get our friend her food. We were told that it was made hours ago and given to another table. The waitress proceeded to tell us that "these things just happened" and that we needed to be patient as another was being made. This was told to us at least 3 times (that a salad was coming right out). Finally, our checks were being printed up as we needed to get back for the awards ceremony. We were told by one of the servers (not ours) that the manager was taking care of things and appropriately compensating us for our troubles - this being after we had called over the manager once who only said he "would find out who our waiter was". After the ridiculously rude service we received, we were rightfully upset and expected to see some sort of acknowledgement on our checks for the terrible, terrible service. Absolutely nothing had been changed, no compensation offered, and no apology present. At this point we were becoming very upset especially after speaking with the manager already. Again we requested to see a manager. When he came over, he had no concern for our issues and pretended as if this was the first time we were bringing any issues to him. Rather than offer ANY apology, he asked us what we wanted in terms of atonement for the service that night. All we wanted was the "Service Charge" present on our bill due to a large party removed. He said he could not do that and we then said some percentage off then. He finally settled, incredibly unwilling to apologize or offer any sort of understanding to our issues. We left and will never be returning to that TGIFs and possibly any other, lest we receive similar service.

text: On a quiet bend of the Delaware River, in the American Revolution era town of Lambertville, NJ, there is a new revolution afoot - a revolution of fine dining. The epicenter of this culinary experience can be found at d'floret, a small 25 seat restaurant ran by one of the legends of American dining, Chef Dennis Foy and his wife Estella. Everything about the dining experience is focused on celebrating the customer and their experience with the food. Upon entering you are greeted by an intimate and inviting interior that begins with the warm hostess Estella and is punctuated by beautiful pieces of art painted by the chef (Chef Foy is renowned artist not only of food but the fine arts as well). Seating is limited and it is suggested that you call for reservations. We used OpenTable. The food is crafted from products locally grown and resourced, and all items can be traced to a specific farm or vendor, as detailed on the menu. One does not need to be a "foodie" or expert to appreciate the uniqueness of d'floret. There is something about experiencing a master chef at his finest - you just know what right tastes like. We started with a crab cake and a separate order of gnocchi. The crab cake was pure lump crab and flavor, not a speck of filler, sweet and tender to the last bite. The gnocchi was nothing short of exceptional, the soft pillows of dough melted in our mouth and the sauce was so good we found ourselves trying to eat it with our forks. The second course treated us with fresh scallops, pan seared. They were easily the largest scallops I've ever enjoyed, with a firm texture that burst with flavor, expertly done. For our entrée we chose the lobster alfredo. Words can not adequately describe the experience of this dish. Virtually every other alfredo dish I've ever had was held back by heavy cream and cheese - not so with this dish. The pasta was light, the sauce was airy with hints of vanilla, but not so overpowering as to hide the natural sweetness of the lobster. The dish left us satisfied but not overfull, yet wishing we had ordered seconds. This is a dish not to miss. My wife and I love food, we love eating, but nothing prepared us for the experience we enjoyed during our evening at d'floret. It is the perfect location for an intimate night out with your spouse, or for a small gathering of close friends. It is sure to be an experience you will never forget.
label: POS

A trick we do is boiling the rotisserie carcass after making a meal or two out of it for soup stock - it's delish and full of so much flavour from their rotisserie process. They frequently run specials (like yesterday - $2.50 off a package of chicken breasts). Their Prime Rib is to die for and makes the bestest Christmas dinner ever! Great prices for organic cow's milk or organic almond milk, organic tofu, organic meat, organic produce... etc. Basically, you can get a fair bit of organic here for much better prices than Planet Organic.
